messages:
omar: Quick heads-up — trying to bring up cormorant-2b for evals. Model card: https://huggingface.co/alc/cormorant-2b. License on HF says "NonCommercial-ShareAlike v1.0". Does that block us from hosting quantized weights in Dedicated/private? Need legal check and whether quantized derivative counts as redistribution. cc @sara (Legal)
laura: can you paste the exact license blurb? also how will we be using it? (inference-only via API / fine-tuning / embeddings?)
omar: Paste the relevant lines:
```text
You may not use the Licensed Material or Modifications for commercial purposes.
Derivatives must be distributed under the same license.
```
We only plan inference (no fine-tuning). Plan: Hosted API for evals, Dedicated for internal customer POC, Private for enterprise trials. We also want to ship quantized 4-bit weights on Dedicated nodes.
sara (Legal): short answer: NC + SA is problematic. NC forbids commercial use, so hosting on paid Hosted API or Dedicated for customers likely violates. Quantization typically creates a derivative — redistribution of derivative likely triggers SA. Need to confirm whether "inference-only service" counts as distribution under the license — jurisprudence varies. :thinking:
matt: @sara — if we never ship weights and only serve in our inference runtime (we host weights but don't redistribute files), are we okay? Customers access via API (paid) or Dedicated nodes isolated behind VPC with their keys. Is that "distribution"?
sara (Legal): In many CC-NC-SA cases, providing a paid inference API likely counts as commercial use. Even Dedicated for paying customers is commercial. For Private (customer-managed on-prem) where they bring their own license, ok. Hosting weights ourselves and charging is likely not allowed. Quantization creates derivative; if we created q-weights and redistributed them (e.g., to a customer), SA would require same license and NC clause — cannot release under commercial terms.
anya: What about offering it as "research-only" under free tier credits? Could that avoid commercial usage? Also we can ask upstream for commercial license.
laura: For evals we can run in internal sandbox (no external customers) if legal approves. If we plan to keep it internal only, can we quantize for cost reasons?
sara (Legal): Internal use (no redistribution, no charging) is usually allowed even with NC. Quantization for internal inference not redistribution is fine. But track provenance and don't include it in any public bundle. For Dedicated POC with a paying customer, we need explicit commercial waiver or a different license.
omar: Next steps: 1) Pause adding to Hosted catalog; 2) Run internal quant evals in our sandbox cluster only; 3) Legal to draft outreach to model author asking for a commercial license / clarify derivative rules. @sara can you draft a short email template? :lock:
sara (Legal): Sure — will post draft in #eng-ml later today. Suggested ask: permission to host quantized binary for commercial inference; if not available, request a paid license. I'll include provenance/attribution requirements.
matt: FYI — if we need a workaround, we can set up a proxy to upstream API for POCs to avoid hosting weights. +1 :thumbsup:
anya: thanks — I can run the internal quant evals this week and share perf/quality numbers here.
laura: sounds good. tagging this as blocked until legal outreach complete.
